why: ModulusCoder.cpp and t_moduluscoder.cpp were written together from one reading of 0x31ff0-0x323c5, so a green run says they agree. The claims are: seven words and not six or eight, all of them cleared, the clear starting at +0x00, and the decoder being the encoder's twin rather than a copy that drifted. The fixture seeds every byte non-zero and reseeds each trial, which is the only reason a dropped initialiser is visible at all -- over a zero-filled slot every entry below would survive.
